questions.question:
Select the correct collocation to fill in the blank.

The teacher gave the students _______ instructions before the exam.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**clear**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**clear**" means easy to understand, free of ambiguity. (स्पष्ट)
 
• Giving clear instructions ensures that the students understand what is expected of them during the exam.
 
• The other options: "**strong**," "**great**," and "**careful**" do not fit the context as appropriately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *The teacher gave the students clear__ instructions before the exam.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Strong (मजबूत)**: means having great physical power.
 
• **Great (महान)**: means of an extent, amount, or intensity considerably above the normal or average.
 
• **Careful (सावधान)**: means making sure of avoiding potential danger, mishap, or harm; cautious.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The dog ran _____ the garden chasing the cat.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**across**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition "across" is used to indicate movement from one side to another side of a place or area.
 
• In this context, the dog is running from one side of the garden to the other while chasing the cat.
 
• The other options: "at," "on," and "between" do not fit the context as appropriately.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *The dog ran across__ the garden chasing the cat.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **At**: used to indicate a specific location or point.
 
• **On**: used to indicate a position above something and in contact with it.
 
• **Between**: used to indicate a position in the middle of two points.

When it comes to cooking, she can really think __creatively and unconventionally__ to create unique dishes that surprise everyone.
questions.solution:

• **Example:** When it comes to marketing strategies, she always thinks creatively and unconventionally to come up with unique campaigns that stand out.
 
 
 
• **"Think outside the box"** is an idiom that describes the ability to think creatively, unorthodoxly, or from a new perspective. (नए दृष्टिकोण से सोचना)
 
 
• **Example:** Successful entrepreneurs often think outside the box to develop groundbreaking products and services.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate idiom to substitute the underlined segment is **'think outside the box'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Outside the wire** (तार के बाहर): Typically refers to being beyond a secured or safe area, often used in military contexts.

 
 
• **Example:** The soldiers were instructed not to venture outside the wire after dark.
 
 
 
• **Outside the canvas** (कैनवास के बाहर): Not a commonly used idiom, could imply thinking beyond the usual artistic boundaries.
 
 
• **Example:** The artist was known for her unique style, always thinking outside the canvas.
 
 
 
• **Outside the law** (कानून के बाहर): Refers to actions that are illegal or not within the bounds of the law.
 
 
• **Example:** The vigilante operated outside the law, taking justice into his own hands.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

(A) He spoke passionately about his favourite book, / (B) articulating his thoughts clear / (C) and engaging everyone in a lively discussion / (D) about its themes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect form of the adjective. The word "clear" should be "clearly" to correctly modify the verb "articulating".
 
• Adverbs are used to modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, and in this case, "clearly" is the appropriate adverbial form.
 
• The correct phrase should be "articulating his thoughts clearly," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part B** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He spoke passionately about his favourite book, articulating his thoughts clearly and engaging everyone in a lively discussion about its themes."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "He spoke passionately about his favourite book," **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **C: "and engaging everyone in a lively discussion" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **D: "about its themes." **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
